topic.title: Scalable Monte Carlo and Structured Bayesian Sampling
topic.overview: Monte Carlo inference explores a probability distribution through random transitions or weighted samples. This topic develops methods that exploit geometry, auxiliary variables, subsampling, and adaptive proposals to make Bayesian computation practical. It distinguishes algorithms with the correct invariant distribution from approximations whose computational savings introduce persistent bias.
topic.whyItMatters: Exactness is a property of the sampling construction, not a guarantee that a short run has explored the posterior adequately. Practical inference must also consider mixing, per-step cost, and diagnostics, especially when target evaluations are expensive or the number of model parameters can change.
topic.evolution: A 1997 reversible-jump method samples Gaussian mixtures with an unknown component count. Later work develops manifold and Hamiltonian dynamics and stochastic-gradient recipes. Scalable Metropolis-Hastings in 2019 reduces average data processing while preserving the target posterior; a 2026 auxiliary-variable framework unifies methods for targets that are difficult even to evaluate.
openQuestions: How can practitioners assess exploration when exact target evaluations are unavailable?
Which geometric or auxiliary-variable constructions improve mixing without excessive per-step work?
